3.
The aforesaid crime was registered pursuant to the FIR lodged by Respondent No.2.
The marriage of Respondent No.2 and Petitioner No.1 was solemnised on 21/01/2014.
Respondent No.2 lodged the FIR on 04/02/2019 alleging that her husband and his family members have subjected her to cruelty.

4. Learned counsel for the Petitioners and Respondent No.2 state that the parties have settled the dispute amicaly and they have filed the consent terms before the Family Court, Bandra in Marriage petition No.F-3742 of 2022.

Copy of the consent terms is placed on record at Exhibit 'C'.
5.
Learned counsel for the Petitioners states that in terms of clause 4 of the consent terms, the Petitioners have deposited an amount of Rs.20,00,000/- before the Family Court.

Both parties have agreed to dissolve the marriage with consent under Section 13(B) of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955 and Respondent No.2 has also agreed to withdraw the cases and to give consent to quash the criminal cases filed against the Petitioners.
Respondent No.2 is present before the Court.
She has been identified by her Advocate.
She confirms that the matter has been settled amicably and that she has no objection to quash the FIR and the criminal proceedings arising therefrom.
7. We are of the considered view that the settlement is voluntary and genuine.
Since the parties have put an end to their matrimonial dispute, continuance of criminal proceedings would be an abuse of process of law.
Hence, this is a fit case to exercise powers under Article 226 of the Constitution of India to secure the ends of justice.
8. Under the circumstances, the petition is allowed in terms of prayer clause (a).

The FIR No.42 of 2019 registered with Naya Nagar Police station, District-Thane for the offences punishable under Sections 323, 324, 354-A, 376, 406, 498-A, 504 and 506 r/w 34 of the IPC and the Regular Criminal Case No.2057 of 2020 arising therefrom and pending on the file of 6th Jt. J.M.F.C., Thane,
stand quashed.

(N.R. BORKAR, J.) (SMT. ANUJA PRABHUDESSAI, J.)
